units.function: Minimal CLI adapter registration for type `http`; trims each raw stdout event and prints any non-empty line unchanged.
units.dependencyDirection: The adapter depends only on the shared CLIAdapterModule type and console output. It is registered by the CLI adapter registry; it has no HTTP client, schema parser, transport lifecycle, capability declaration or test of its own.
units.keyDataModels: Adapter type string `http`, raw stdout string and ignored debug boolean.
units.lifecycle: Receive a raw event string; trim surrounding whitespace; discard empty input; write remaining content to stdout.
units.testAssessment: No focused tests were found for this 11-line unit. CLI no-emit TypeScript passed on 2026-08-19. Empty/non-empty behavior is obvious from source, but escaping, binary/large input, redaction, structured event parsing, error routing and debug semantics are entirely unverified.
units.designRationale: Provide a fallback presentation adapter for HTTP runtimes whose output is already human-readable, avoiding provider-specific parsing in the CLI.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS Connectors must emit stable structured progress/evidence/result/error events with version, sequence, run identity, classification and runtime proof; operator CLI rendering is a separate concern.
units.companyOsFit: REJECT as a Connector or evidence reference. A raw passthrough may exist only in an internal diagnostic view after server-side classification/redaction and explicit untrusted-output labeling. Company OS should render normalized Connector events, not treat arbitrary stdout as the event contract.
units.responsibilityConflict: Raw stdout has no requester, accountable human, Work/contract, permission/data scope, approval, evidence digest, result identity or runtime attestation and therefore cannot enter the responsibility chain as authoritative evidence.

securityFindings: Arbitrary runtime stdout is printed unchanged after trim, with no Secret/path/token/private-session redaction or content classification.
Terminal control sequences, escape injection, misleading formatting and log-forging content are not neutralized.
No size/rate/backpressure bound exists at this adapter surface, so high-volume or huge lines can degrade terminals/log collectors.
The debug parameter is ignored and no distinction exists between customer-safe output and privileged diagnostics.
No stable event schema, version, sequence, timestamp, source, severity, evidence digest or completeness marker is parsed or displayed.
Calling the unit `http` can imply a transport boundary, but it performs presentation only; ownership naming is ambiguous.
